title: Video by rndyrbrts
description:
What’s the first thing you’d run through a model that shows you how content targets your brain?

Last video I showed you TRIBE v2 — Meta’s brain prediction model — and used it to write a paragraph that matched the neural fingerprint of Clair de Lune. A lot of you said the same thing: if you can target a specific emotional response with text, someone is going to weaponize that. You’re right. They will.

But the same model works in reverse.

Right now, if a headline is engineered to make you angry, the only way to know is to notice your own reaction after it already got you. TRIBE reads the other direction. Content goes in — video, audio, language — and predicted brain response comes out. Amygdala activation, prefrontal suppression, emotional hijacking signatures. Mapped, readable, quantifiable, visible before you ever click play.

Imagine a browser extension. You’re scrolling, every piece of content already scanned, and next to each one a small readout of what it’s designed to do to your brain.

TRIBE can be used two ways. One direction, you write content that targets a feeling. The other direction, you see the targeting happening. The second one is much bigger, because manipulation only works in the dark.

What happens to the internet when the lights come on?
